The aim of the MER PF is to detect objects in the \Euclid imaging data, measure their properties, and combine them into a single multi-wavelength catalogue. In this paper we illustrate the design of the MER PF and introduce the different photometric methods applied to the data, which are Kron total flux, aperture photometry on Point Spread Functions (PSF) -matched images, template fitting photometry, and Sérsic fitting photometry. We also present the various morphological measurements and quality flags that improve the scientific content of the output catalogues and better characterize the detected sources. We illustrate the processing and measurements that help to validate the MER PF results, which is an essential step to qualify the output for the public DR1 release. We discuss the global assessment of the photometric homogeneity and provide an internal comparison of our processing results. In addition, we give an extensive overview of the DR1 output data and the various processing scenarios

papers.title: Squeezing Drives Southward Magnetic Field Enhancement During 10 May 2024 CME-CME Interaction
papers.abstract: The southward magnetic field carried by coronal mass ejections (CMEs) is a key driver of space weather events, yet how interacting CMEs amplify this field remains debated. The 10 May 2024 event, which produced the strongest geomagnetic storm since 2003, offers an ideal testbed for this question. Combining multi-spacecraft observations with high-resolution controlled numerical experiments, we track the CMEs continuously from their origin near the solar surface to beyond Earth, and find that inherent squeezing during CME-CME interactions generates the sustained enhancement of the southward field, exceeding 60 nT in magnitude near Earth. First driven by the dynamic pressure of the trailing CME and later maintained by magnetic and thermal pressures at the CME-CME interface, squeezing transforms the preceding CME from a bulky cloud into a flattened "pancake" structure, prevents expansion-induced field decay, and maintains an amplified southward field over long distances. The strength of this enhancement scales with the intensity of the squeezing. Our findings establish a direct link between CME-CME interaction and strong southward fields, laying a physics-based foundation for understanding and forecasting the geoeffectiveness of interacting CMEs.

papers.title: Periodic Modulation of Linear Polarization Fraction in Repeating FRB 20240114A
papers.abstract: Long-term polarization changes in repeating fast radio bursts (FRBs) can probe their emission geometry and propagation environment. We searched for periodic variation in the degree of linear polarization (DOL) of FRB~20240114A using the polarization catalog from the Five-hundred-meter Aperture Spherical radio Telescope. The sample contains 6,099 bursts detected on 95 observing days over $\sim 488$ days. The daily mean DOL series was analyzed using phase distance correlation and Lomb--Scargle periodograms over trial periods of 10--240 days. The strongest peaks occur at $119.91^{+2.67}_{-2.04}$ and $122.31^{+2.63}_{-2.82}$ days, respectively. The quoted ranges correspond to the period intervals above the global $3σ$ thresholds. Global false-alarm probabilities were estimated from \(10^7\) random permutations of the daily values among the fixed observing dates, with the full period search repeated for each permutation. The resulting probabilities are \(9.98\times10^{-4}\) and \(8.95\times10^{-4}\), corresponding to equivalent Gaussian significances of \(3.09σ\) and \(3.12σ\), respectively. As a supplementary check, the same analysis using daily median DOL yielded similar peaks near 120 days. A descriptive sinusoidal fit to all 95 daily mean DOL measurements at a fixed period of 119.91 days has a semi-amplitude of 3.23\%. Possible explanations include precession-driven changes in viewing geometry and variations in propagation conditions within a binary system.

papers.title: Counter-rotating Ionized and Neutral Gas in a Star-forming Elliptical Galaxy
papers.abstract: In early-type galaxies, gas that is kinematically misaligned with the stars generally rotates together across all gas phases, implying a single external origin. Using upgraded Giant Metrewave Radio Telescope (uGMRT) 21 cm imaging and SDSS-MaNGA spatially resolved spectroscopy, we studied MaNGA 10214-1902, a compact ($R_e = 0.78$ kpc), star-forming elliptical galaxy with stellar mass $\log M_*/M_{\odot} = 9.90$, in which the ionized gas counter-rotates with respect to the stars. It hosts $\log(M_{\rm HI}/M_{\odot}) = 9.65$ in a 45 kpc HI disk that co-rotates with the stars and has a central column-density depression. Inside this depression, the ionized gas ($r \lesssim 2$ kpc) rotates in the opposite sense to both the stars ($Δ{\rm PA} = 152^\circ \pm 20^\circ$) and the HI that surrounds it ($Δ{\rm PA} = 179^\circ \pm 10^\circ$). HI co-spatial with the ionized gas is not detected, so a fainter inner HI component with a different orientation cannot be ruled out. This central gas is star-forming in the [SII] and [OI] diagnostic diagrams and has EW(HI) $>6~\mathrm{\mathring{A}}$ at the center. The 1.4 GHz radio-continuum star formation rate agrees with the spectral energy distribution based value, showing no evidence of a dominant active galactic nucleus. The stellar population at the center is younger than the outskirts and has the lowest D$_{\rm n}$4000. These results are consistent with the acquisition of gas with opposite angular momentum into the center of a pre-existing HI disk that co-rotates with the stars, which can fuel the most recent central star formation.

papers.title: Axion quintessence with a negative cosmological constant: Bayesian constraints from current cosmological data
papers.abstract: We constrain canonical axion quintessence with a negative cosmological constant using DES Year 5 supernovae, DESI DR2 BAO, compressed CMB information, and geometry-corrected Gold-2017 growth data. We solve the background and linear-growth equations and sample with PolyChord. Our joint prior is logarithmic in the decay constant over $0.005\leq f/M_{\rm Pl}\leq10$ and uniform in the initial angle $θ_i=φ_i/f\in[0,π]$, conditioned on $π-θ_i\geq H_{\rm inf}/(2πf)$ with $H_{\rm inf}=10^{13}$ GeV and reduced Planck mass $M_{\rm Pl}$. The broad-prior model favors recent thawing, with median $w_{{\rm DE},0}=-0.865^{+0.068}_{-0.053}$, $m_φ\in[0.91,4.39]\times10^{-33}$ eV, and $f/M_{\rm Pl}\in[0.589,4.899]$ (central 68\% credible intervals). Bayes factors relative to flat $Λ$CDM are 0.70 and 30.1 for the normalized fluctuation-conditioned prior (Convention I) and its further conditioning on numerical acceptance (Convention II). Restricting $f\leq M_{\rm Pl}$ gives $f/M_{\rm Pl}\in[0.262,0.822]$ at 68\% credibility and Bayes factors 0.233 and 32.4. Relative to the zero-vacuum axion model, the broad-prior Bayes factors are 0.620 and 1.65, providing no compelling evidence for a negative cosmological constant. Local likelihood optimization gives an Akaike information criterion difference $Δ{\rm AIC}\simeq-10.87$ for the zero-vacuum model relative to flat $Λ$CDM. For this model, assuming that the instanton generating $m_φ^2f^2=Λ_{\rm UV}^4e^{-S_{\rm inst}}$ satisfies the axionic Weak Gravity Conjecture, the one-sided 95\% posterior lower limit on the minimum compatible coefficient $c_{\min}$ rises from 37 to 55 as the ultraviolet scale $Λ_{\rm UV}$ increases from $10^{-10}M_{\rm Pl}$ to $M_{\rm Pl}$, in tension with an order-one coefficient under these assumptions.

papers.title: Predicting Individual Dark Matter Halo Concentrations from Their Assembly Histories
papers.abstract: We present an empirical model for predicting concentration parameters of individual dark matter halos in cold and warm dark matter (WDM) cosmologies over z=0-5. Constructed using a large suite of cosmological N-body simulations, our model separately incorporates cosmic expansion (linear growth factor), mass scale (linear density fluctuations), halo mass assembly histories via the Extended Press-Schechter (EPS) scaled formation variable, plus a WDM damping term tied to the half-mode mass. It works for both virial and 200 $ρ_{crit}$ halo definitions. Across all tested cosmologies and redshifts, our global logarithmic fit gives concentration scatter ~0.09 dex for relaxed halos and ~0.09 to 0.10 dex for all halos. While relaxed halos maintain nearly constant scatter near 0.09 dex, the scatter of all halos at z>3 increases from 0.10 to 0.18 dex, revealing substantial violent-relaxation impacts on high-redshift halo structure. At fixed mass, concentration scatter is dominated by assembly history. We extract the scaled formation variable's probability distribution function (PDF) from merger trees and find departures from standard EPS theory. This PDF is narrower in WDM than LCDM due to suppressed small-scale perturbations and rapid, delayed monolithic collapse near the WDM truncation scale. Monte Carlo realizations with our formulae reproduce concentration distributions and match our prior peak-concentration model, whereas standard EPS underestimates concentrations from delayed-formation bias. Our framework offers a transparent, computationally lightweight tool to predict individual halo concentrations across diverse cosmological models.

papers.title: On the Existence of a Third Planet and an Apsidal Resonance Chain in the Kepler-396 System through TESS Data
papers.abstract: The possible existence of a third planet in the Kepler-396 system has been previously proposed. Given that the planetary mass is poorly constrained and the orbit could be either interior or exterior to planet Kepler-396 c, that proposal is not clearly known in the community. In order to address this and further investigate Kepler-396 system's configuration, new TESS data are employed to form a long baseline of transit timing. Using the pixel-level decorrelation technique, the mid-transit times are determined. Through long baseline transit-timing-variation technique, we perform a comprehensive exploration of the parameter space of the third planet. Two best-fit solutions, derived from different priors of orbital inclinations, have led to the reduced chi-square values as 2.24 and 2.34 respectively, compared to 12.97 for the two-planet model. This result strongly suggests the existence of the third planet, i.e. Kepler-396 d. Based on these two best-fit solutions, the masses of Kepler-396 b, c, d are updated to be around 9, 4, 4 Earth Mass, and the corresponding orbital periods are 43, 89, 144 days, respectively. With these updated masses, Kepler-396 b is on the border between rocky or volatile-rich, Kepler-396 c is confirmed to be a volatile-rich super-puff planet, and both planets lie in the Neptune savanna. Dynamical simulations with three planets are performed, showing that they are stable for a timescale of $10^6$ years. The examination on resonant angles leads to the conclusion that planets Kepler-396 b, c, d form a three-body apsidal resonance chain.

papers.title: SN Progenitors of SNRs in OB Associations in the LMC. I. Assessment of Methodology Using N63A
papers.abstract: Color--magnitude diagrams (CMDs) can constrain the progenitor masses of supernova remnants (SNRs), but mass estimates for massive stars are affected by limited temperature sensitivity, extinction, crowding, and nebular contamination. We use the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC) SNR N63A and its OB association LH83 as a benchmark to evaluate CMD-based mass estimates. Among the tested diagnostics, the extinction-corrected MCPS $B$ vs. $U-B$ CMD provides the most useful constraint on the massive-star population. The $V$ vs. $B-V$ CMD is less reliable, while the reddening-free $W$-$Q$ diagram does not improve individual mass estimates because of its larger photometric uncertainties. Gaia EDR3 recovers bright stars missing or saturated in MCPS but provides weaker separation among the hottest stars. For seven spectroscopically classified stars, the $B$ vs. $U-B$ CMD-based masses are lower than the HR-diagram masses inferred using the same MIST tracks by $8.0~M_\odot$ on average, with a scatter of $7.0~M_\odot$. Isochrone comparisons suggest that most of the massive stars in LH83 formed about 7-15 Myr ago, complicating progenitor mass estimates based on the present-day mass function. Nevertheless, the masses of D243-1a and D243-2, stellar lifetimes predicted by the MIST models, and the empirical bubble-size-progenitor-mass relation suggest a progenitor mass of order 25-30 $M_\odot$. Our results highlight the potential and limitations of this approach for studying other LMC SNRs in OB associations.

papers.title: $^8$B Solar Neutrino Measurements of Solar Core Size and Temperature from 5805 Days of Super-Kamiokande
papers.abstract: The detection of solar neutrino provides direct evidence for on-going fusion in the core of the Sun and serve as a probe for that solar core. Production rate of $^8$B is sensitive to the solar core temperature. Adiabatic flavor conversion of $^8$B solar neutrinos depends on the local solar electron density. Combined with the roughly exponential decrease in solar electron density with increasing distance from the center of the solar sphere, the solar core size, density, and temperature are inferred. This article presents an outer bound on solar core size and measurements of the density and temperature in the solar core based on Super-Kamiokande phase I-IV solar neutrino data. An outer bound is set for the solar core at $90\%$ confidence level as $0.499R_\odot$ for the high metallicity B16+GS98 Standard Solar Model and $0.381R_\odot$ for K2-A09-MZvar-12 which includes protosolar accretion. A combined fit with the SNO polynomial coefficients improves the limit to $0.268R_\odot$ for B16+GS98 and $0.215R_\odot$ for K2-A09-MZvar-12. Results for other metallicity cases are also reported. In the high metallicity scenario assuming nominal solar core density and solar core size, temperature at the solar center is reported at $T_\text{C}=(15.599\pm0.0016)\times10^6$ K and $T_{\text{npz}}=(15.492\pm0.0017)\times10^6$ K at the peak radius of the $^8$B production profile.

papers.title: DART ejecta reveal the recoil momentum budget of a kinetic impact
papers.abstract: Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) demonstrated that ejecta recoil enhances asteroid deflection, but the ejecta processes generating and distributing this recoil remained unclear. We reconstruct three-dimensional ejecta evolution from time-resolved morphology and brightness observations, recovering previously missing constraints on momentum transfer and material transport. Integrating reconstructed momentum yields momentum enhancement factors $β_\mathrm{D}=2.13 \pm 0.19 (1σ)$ for Dimorphos and $β_\mathrm{sys}=2.04 \pm 0.19 (1σ)$ for the Didymos system. Combined with the measured deflection, the reconstructed recoil constrains Dimorphos's bulk density to $1435.18_{-153.71}^{+112.59} \mathrm{kg m^{-3}}$ without assuming its mass. By linking observed orbital deflection to the released material, this reconstruction provides ejecta-based constraints for assessing kinetic-impact effectiveness and investigating how natural collisions drive mass loss and debris transport among small Solar System bodies.

papers.title: Polarization of strongly lensed gravitational waves as a probe of the lens-induced orientations of electromagnetic counterparts
papers.abstract: Strong gravitational lensing is a well-established phenomenon in electromagnetic (EM) observations, where the lensed images and arcs are resolved on the two-dimensional sky and constrain the mass distribution of the lens. Strongly lensed gravitational waves (GWs) are also expected to be detected routinely by next-generation detectors, but their multiple images are recorded only as one-dimensional time series without positions. Among them, lensed binary neutron star mergers can be accompanied by EM counterparts with resolvable structures, such as relativistic jets. In EM lensing, the lens-induced change in the apparent orientation of such a structure can be measured only relative to other images or statistically, because its intrinsic orientation is not directly observable. In this work, we show that the GW polarization, which the lens leaves unchanged, provides this missing reference, i.e., a compass, so that the orientation offset of each image can be measured in absolute terms. We place this orientation layer on the EM image plane together with image positions from the lensed host arcs and Fermat-potential heights from GW time delays and magnifications. Using a mock population of such mergers observable by the Einstein Telescope and Cosmic Explorer, we find that the predicted image positions and arrival times are calibrated once the detection selection is included. The lens-induced orientation offsets reach tens of degrees and are detectable in up to a third of the events, at viewing angles above about $40^\circ$ for quadrupole-dominated signals.

papers.title: Calibrated Period-Luminosity Relations for Mira variables in the Large Magellanic Cloud in the Vera C. Rubin Observatory $zy$-band Photometric Systems
papers.abstract: The Vera C. Rubin Observatory's Legacy Survey of Space Time (LSST) is expected to discover numerous Mira variables in nearby galaxies, enabling their application for the cosmic distance scale. Miras are excellent distance indicators at infrared wavelengths, and therefore their period-luminosity (PL) relations in reddest $zy$ photometric systems will be crucial in the LSST era. We present first empirical $zy$-band PL relation for 85 oxygen-rich (O-rich) Miras located in the Large Magellanic Cloud based on time-series observations collected using the Dark Energy Camera (DECam) at the Víctor M. Blanco 4-m Telescope. The DECam photometry was directly calibrated using the Rubin Observatory Data Preview 2 (DP2) data. The observed PL relations were found to exhibit a break around a period of $\sim 300$ days, and therefore we only derived and calibrated the PL relations for Miras with a period shorter than $300$ days. We also explored the Rubin LSST DP2 data for known Mira variables in three Local Group dwarf galaxies. The $zy$-band light curves of Miras in IC 1613 are too sparsely sampled, whereas the DP2 observations of NGC 6822 and the Sagittarius Dwarf Irregular Galaxy cover only a short temporal baseline. For an O-rich Mira in NGC 6822, we obtain a distance modulus $μ= 23.32\pm0.24$~mag in good agreement with the literature. Significantly improved temporal coverage is expected in the first official Rubin LSST data release that will enable a robust validation of the PL relation in these nearby systems.

papers.title: Resonant Trapping of Neutrinophilic Dark Matter in Supernovae
papers.abstract: Supernova cooling provides some of the strongest constraints on light particles beyond the Standard Model, including sub-GeV dark matter (DM). While sufficiently large couplings to the Standard Model sector can trap these particles inside the supernova or cause them to decay before escaping, there typically exists an intermediate range of couplings in which their efficient production and subsequent escape lead to excessive energy loss, resulting in stringent constraints on new light particles. In this work, we demonstrate for the first time that, for certain types of DM-neutrino interactions, resonantly enhanced $s$-channel scattering with neutrinos can efficiently trap DM inside the supernova and can fundamentally alter the conventional supernova cooling constraints. In particular, we show that for mediator masses comparable to the supernova core temperature, this resonant scattering can prevent a substantial fraction of the produced DM from freely escaping, thereby significantly weakening, or even evading, the usual supernova cooling constraints on such models.

papers.title: Observations of stellar feedback: tracers, diagnostics, measurements, and physical interpretation
papers.abstract: Stellar feedback is central to galaxy evolution, yet the coupling of radiation, stellar winds, and supernovae to the multi-phase interstellar medium remains uncertain. This review treats this as a problem of inference, framed around four qualitative axes of ignorance: observational diagnostics are indirect; stellar population synthesis models must be ground-truthed before being used to infer feedback quantities; recent high-redshift observations have opened a new regime that may require re-calibration; and stellar feedback and the affected environment are interdependent. We examine the inference chain, from observables to physical quantities and from those quantities to how energy and momentum are transferred to the surrounding medium, across the principal diagnostics of stellar feedback: ionised gas, mechanically-driven bubbles, giant molecular cloud lifetimes, galactic outflows, and Lyman-continuum escape. We ask how much observations reveal about the link between the feedback-driving massive stars and the feedback-driven interstellar medium. We further discuss how stellar population synthesis assumptions, environment (e.g., metallicity, dust content), and galaxy properties (e.g., stellar mass, gas content) affect feedback measurements, and how high-redshift observations are testing calibrations established in the nearby Universe. The emerging picture is that interpreting a feedback measurement requires explicit control of the inference chain and of its physical context; feedback should therefore be contextualised, i.e. interpreted in terms of mechanism, gas phase, environment, and spatial and temporal scale. Progress will depend on measuring feedback-related quantities across the full range of star-forming systems and, more importantly, on obtaining observations (real, and synthetic from post-processed simulations) that match the same tracer and spatial scale across the same systems.

papers.title: Detectability limits of Ce abundances in Gaia RVS
papers.abstract: Gaia DR3 provides medium-resolution Radial Velocity Spectrograph (RVS) spectra for millions of stars, but the extent to which they contain recoverable cerium (Ce) information across stellar parameter space remains unclear. We assess Ce detectability in Gaia RVS spectra and the reliability of DR3 Ce abundances ahead of the larger DR4 catalogue. We compute synthetic spectra across a stellar-parameter grid representative of the Gaia RVS sample. We combine the Cayrel equivalent-width criterion and the Cramér-Rao bound to map Ce detectability as a function of stellar parameters and signal-to-noise (SNR). We also quantify continuum-placement errors and compare the predicted detectability boundary with the Gaia DR3 GSP-Spec catalogue. Ce is reliably detectable primarily in cool giants at [Fe/H] $\gtrsim$ 0.5 dex and with at least [Ce/Fe] $\gtrsim$ 0 at an average SNR of 50, and the detectability region expands toward higher gravities at increasing SNR. Continuum-placement errors of $\gtrsim$1% become a significant source of bias, and at $\gtrsim$2% they completely prevent Ce detection. The criterion we present identifies where RVS Ce abundances, including those from DR4, can be robustly exploited. Outside our detectability region, these abundances should be interpreted cautiously, whether derived by GSP-Spec or by supervised methods. Currently, depending on the assumed continuum-placement uncertainty, between $\sim$40% and $\sim$70% of the published DR3 Ce measurements fall within this region; however, the rest are not reliable. Our findings are particularly important for metal-poor stars, for which the Ce lines in the RVS range are simply not detectable.

papers.title: The Eclipsing $δ$ Scuti Binary HIP 7666: Absolute Dimensions and Pulsation Properties
papers.abstract: We present a comprehensive analysis of the pulsating eclipsing binary HIP 7666 (TIC 308953703), containing a $δ$ Sct-type component, based on 120-s TESS photometry and 63 newly acquired high-resolution echelle spectra. While previous orbital solutions were limited by sparse spectroscopic sampling, our extensive radial velocity (RV) measurements enable a robust determination of the system's physical parameters. The primary has an effective temperature of $T_{\rm eff,A}$ = 7376$\pm$72 K and a projected rotational velocity of $v_{\rm A}\sin i$ = 56.6$\pm$5.3 km s$^{-1}$. Joint modeling of the light and RV curves shows that HIP 7666 is a detached system in a circular orbit, with Roche-lobe filling factors of $f_{\rm A}$ = 57 \% and $f_{\rm B}$ = 44 \%. The masses and radii are determined to better than 2 \% precision: $M_{\rm A}$ = 1.822$\pm$0.029 $M_\odot$, $R_{\rm A}$ = 2.154$\pm$0.017 $R_\odot$ for the primary, and $M_{\rm B}$ = 1.246$\pm$0.020 $M_\odot$, $R_{\rm B}$ = 1.170$\pm$0.015 $R_\odot$ for the secondary. The binary-based distance (316$\pm$8 pc) agrees well with the Gaia DR3 parallax-based distance (313$\pm$1 pc), validating the derived system parameters. Frequency analysis of the light-curve residuals reveals 15 significant signals, predominantly in the $δ$ Sct pulsation frequency range. PARSEC evolutionary tracks indicate an age of $\sim$0.9 Gyr and a supersolar metallicity ($Z=0.03$), with the primary on the main sequence and the secondary located close to the zero-age main sequence. Galactic kinematics place HIP 7666 in the thin disk.

papers.title: Hydrodynamic and photoionization analysis of a Cosmic Dawn dwarf galaxy based on a JWST-inferred star formation history
papers.abstract: We investigate the evolution of the emergent spectrum of the Cosmic Dawn dwarf galaxy 2779 using coupled hydrodynamics and photoionization modeling. Evolutionary sequences of spherically symmetric, multi-component models track the star-formation history -- derived from JWST data -- from $z \approx 29.5$ to $9.5$. BPASS stellar population synthesis is coupled with the evolution of the superwind bubble and the surrounding nebular environment. The emergent spectra include escaping stellar radiation, nebular lines and continuum, as well as X-ray emission from the hot superwind cavity. At early stages, the nebular shell suppresses the escape of Lyman-continuum (Lyc) photons, while allowing X-ray emission to emerge. Significant Lyc escape appears near $z \approx 20$, followed by a non-monotonic evolution of the escape fraction ($f_{\text{esc}}$) and the X-ray luminosity per unit star-formation rate ($L_X/\text{SFR}$). Including diffuse ionizing radiation from the nebula can result in an effective escape fraction $f_{\text{esc}} > 1$. The model sequences terminate at a stage of stagnation or the complete displacement of the outer nebular component into a shell. A comparison with JWST photometry indicates that the final model spectrum generally reproduces the shape of the observed spectral energy distribution, although the overall flux level is too high. An illustrative comparison with a previous model having a lower stellar mass indicates that accounting for the evolving contribution of the nebula can reduce the stellar mass required to match observations. However, a more precise determination of stellar mass requires a self-consistent refinement of the star formation history. These models serve as a basis for constructing representative grids of models, as well as for conducting careful checks on whether dwarf galaxies could have driven the reionization of the Universe on their own.

papers.title: Multimessenger Exoplanets: Combining Infrared Excess and Astrometry with Gravitational-wave Detections of Double White Dwarf Exoplanets
papers.abstract: Multimessenger astrophysics provides a powerful framework for characterizing astrophysical systems through multiple, independent signals rather than relying solely on electromagnetic (EM) observations. While most prior multimessenger studies have focused on the properties of ultracompact objects, recent work has shown that gravitational waves (GWs) detectable with the upcoming Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) observatory can also be used to detect exoplanets orbiting stellar remnants. In particular, this includes circumbinary planets around tight double white dwarf (DWD) systems. This population is unique: no such planets are currently known around DWDs, and only a handful of circumbinary planets around main-sequence stars and planets orbiting white dwarfs (WDs) have been identified. Independent EM confirmation will be essential, especially for the first GW-detected exoplanets, to validate this method. While EM techniques are unlikely to efficiently survey large populations of DWDs, GW detection followed by targeted EM confirmation provides one pathway for identifying and characterizing these systems. Using a representative case, the known DWD ZTF J2243+5242 scaled to a fiducial distance of 150 pc, we compute the detectability of circumbinary exoplanets via LISA GW observations. We then demonstrate two complementary EM techniques--JWST infrared (IR) excess and Gaia or Habitable Worlds Observatory astrometry--that could independently confirm a GW-detected planet in this fiducial system. We present the first exploration of IR excess around DWDs as a viable exoplanet detection method, extending its established use for solitary WDs. Both EM techniques overlap with regions of parameter space where LISA is sensitive to DWD exoplanets, enabling robust confirmation and characterization.

papers.title: Receiving Exoplanet Messages with Gravitational-wave Carriers: The Gravitational-wave Radial Velocity Method
papers.abstract: Gravitational-wave (GW) radial velocity (RV) may offer a new method for detecting exoplanets, one that would primarily target planets orbiting GW-emitting, ultracompact, post-main-sequence stellar objects such as white dwarfs, neutron stars, and black holes. In this work we show that while similar to electromagnetic-based RV, this GW-based method depends on the ''phase modulation index'' (PMI), a parameter that is more sensitive to high-mass, long-period exoplanets. We investigate the potential of GW RV for GW sources in both the mid-frequency spectrum (where the upcoming LISA mission will operate) and the high-frequency spectrum (where the current LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK) observatories operate). Remarkably, we find that the PMI increases by a factor of $\sim \mathrm{O}\left(10^4 - 10^6\right)$ going from the mid-frequency to the high-frequency GW spectrum, which results in a greater redistribution of observed power due to the exoplanet's presence. By analyzing the power content of the observed GW signal, we derive analytic expressions to predict the GW carrier frequency power loss due to the exoplanet and the signal-to-noise ratio of the GW source and the exoplanet. We also explore the effects of the additional Doppler effect caused by the motion of the GW observatory and the potential for GW source parameter bias introduced by the presence of an undetected exoplanet. All of this helps us better understand where the GW RV method may work best in the exoplanet mass-period discovery space.

papers.title: Unsupervised learning reveals a small number of galaxy formation pathways in IllustrisTNG
papers.abstract: Understanding the main drivers of galaxy formation and the connection between observable properties and evolutionary pathways is a central goal of extragalactic astronomy. Observations provide single-epoch snapshots of galaxies at different stages of their development, whereas cosmological simulations allow us to trace the full formation histories of individual systems within a theoretical framework. Extracting information from these datasets remains challenging. Our aim is to use machine-learning techniques to unveil physical properties from the simulation datasets. We apply two unsupervised ML techniques, dimensionality reduction and clustering, to identify galaxy evolution key parameters. We use UMAP as our dimensionality reduction tool and k-means as our clustering method. We perform dimensionality reduction on the star formation histories (SFHs) of a sample of aproximately 10000 galaxies drawn from the TNG50 and TNG100 simulations. The resulting representation of the SFHs in a two-dimensional UMAP space reveals a clear ordering of galaxy mass assembly histories, separating quenched and star-forming systems, as well as galaxies with significant ex situ stellar mass contributions. Galaxy properties from simulation catalogs that are not used in the dimensionality reduction show correlations across the UMAP plane. Furthermore, using a k-means clustering analysis, we identify six groups of galaxies with distinct evolutionary histories. These groups show systematic differences in stellar mass, morphology, angular momentum, star formation activity, and merger history, and occupy different regions of the SFR-mass and mass-size planes. Our results indicate that the diversity of galaxy formation histories in IllustrisTNG can be organized into a small number of characteristic evolutionary pathways linking galaxy accretion histories and present-day structural and star-forming properties.

papers.title: Note on quantum optimal measurements of CMB spectral distortions
papers.abstract: As quantum sensing techniques continue to push the frontier of detection of ultra-weak signals, one may wonder if a sophisticated quantum strategy could be used to enable measurement of spectral distortions in the cosmic microwave background. Using quantum Fisher information techniques, we prove that the optimal strategy is simple frequency-binned intensity measurement. This proof strategy also enables us to provide numerical estimates for the information-theoretic minimum observation time required to observe the $μ$- and $y$-distortions expected from $Λ$CDM cosmology. As case studies, we compare these results to the PIXIE and SPECTER mission concepts, and show that they are within a few orders of magnitude of this fundamental limit.

papers.title: Multipoles in the IllustrisTNG simulation galaxies and implications for Strong Gravitational Lens modelling in Time-delay Cosmography
papers.abstract: Time-delay cosmography is a powerful independent probe of the Hubble constant ($H_0$), yet reaching the sub-2$\%$ precision required to resolve the Hubble tension demands a rigorous treatment of mass model systematics. We use realistic massive elliptical galaxies from the IllustrisTNG hydrodynamic simulation suite to characterise higher-order angular mass complexity in the form of multipoles ($m=1,3,4$) and quantify their impact on $H_0$ inference. We find that these multipole perturbations are common and emergent features of galaxy assembly; in 51$\%$ of our total samples ($54\%$ TNG100-1 galaxies and $85\%$ for TNG50-1 galaxies), the addition of multipole terms to a standard elliptical power-law model is preferred by the Bayesian Information Criterion. Ignoring these structures in lens modelling introduces systematic biases in $H_0$: for perturbations of $\sim2\%$, the biases are of the order of 1--2$\%$ for $m=1$, 4--5$\%$ for $m=3$, and 3--6$\%$ for $m=4$ multipole. While the $m=4$ (boxy/discyness) mode induces a predictable directional bias, odd-order modes ($m=1,3$) introduce significant stochastic scatter. We demonstrate a degeneracy where unmodelled internal multipoles can be effectively absorbed by the external shear component. This combined with low signal-to-noise observations can create ``hidden biases'' where formally perfect fits to imaging data ($χ_ν^2 \approx 1$) could harbour significant cosmological errors. Our results provide an astrophysical basis for multipole priors and highlight the necessity of moving beyond rigid parametric models to achieve high-accuracy cosmography in the era of \textit{Euclid} and LSST.

papers.title: Euclid DR1 Legacy Science on Ultracool Dwarfs: New URLD candidates in Euclid and SPHEREx
papers.abstract: Unusually red L dwarfs (URLDs) probe extreme atmospheric conditions in the substellar regime, where enhanced dust opacity, cloud structure, and surface gravity effects challenge standard brown dwarf models. As free-floating analogues of young giant exoplanets, they provide key benchmarks for interpreting low-resolution infrared spectra from current and future wide-field space missions. The goal is to identify new red L dwarf candidates both photometrically and spectroscopically in the first data release (DR1) of the Euclid space mission. The area covered is about 1,900 and 50 square degrees in the wide and deep survey, respectively. We used colour cuts in multiple colour-colour diagrams combined with point-source and quality criteria to identify candidate red L dwarfs in both the Euclid wide and deep survey fields. We cross-matched photometric candidates with the SPHEREx mission and Euclid red grism spectra to confirm spectroscopic properties and evaluate bolometric magnitudes and colours. We identified 1202 and 38 red L dwarf candidates in the Euclid wide and deep surveys, respectively. Spectroscopic follow-up and archival cross-matching confirm a substantial new population of red L dwarfs. Distance-independent diagnostics show that these objects occupy distinct loci characterised by enhanced condensate opacity and significant redness. Euclid vastly expands the census of unusually red L dwarfs. While preliminary spectral classifications suggest many of these new candidates are intermediate-age (Pleiades-like) objects, a subset exhibits extremely red signatures indicative of very young, low-gravity (<=10 Myr) atmospheres, providing vital benchmarks for young exoplanet research.

papers.title: The ISM-CGM Transition of a Star-forming Dwarf Galaxy Resolved in Ionized Gas Emission
papers.abstract: The circumgalactic media (CGM) of dwarf galaxies are expected to be tightly coupled to their star formation, as low virial temperatures imply a CGM rich in cold accretion and shallow potential wells allow for more effective feedback. In this work, we use Keck/KCWI and KCRM to spatially resolve the ionized gas at the boundary between the interstellar medium (ISM) and CGM in dwarf galaxy UGC 6578 (M* = 10^7.8 Msun), out to ~0.1 Rvir. We discover a clear transition between the ISM and CGM at 0.033 Rvir, where the Halpha surface brightness profile changes from an exponential to a shallow power law, marking the first such detection at M*/Msun < 10^8. BPT diagnostics and ionization budget calculations indicate that the gas in the inner CGM is likely ionized by the galaxy's own star formation activity rather than shocks or the UV background. Spatially resolved emission maps also reveal a kinematically distinct, low-metallicity clump embedded in the inner CGM, and we discuss the possibility that this is a direct detection of ongoing gas accretion. This work serves as a pilot study for the Baryon Recycling in Dwarf Galaxies Emission Survey (BRIDGES), which will combine spatially resolved KCWI observations of the ISM-CGM interface in low-mass galaxies with wide-field observations of diffuse ionized gas out to the virial radius with the MOTHRA array.

papers.title: Insights into low-ionization structures in planetary nebulae: near-IR longslit spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Context. Low-ionization structures (LISs) are small, dense clumps within planetary nebulae (PNe) that stand out in low-ionization emission lines, but the physical processes responsible for their excitation and the nature of H2 remain poorly understood. Aims. We aim to characterize the excitation conditions and mass content of LISs in two PNe through near-IR longslit spectroscopy of these structures, combining H2, Brg, and [Fe II] diagnostics. Methods. We obtained H and K band spectra with GNIRS at Gemini North for LISs in NGC 6818 and NGC 7354 --objects with confirmed H2 emission in their LISs. We applied H2 excitation diagrams, vibrational and rotational temperature diagnostics, classical near-IR diagnostic diagrams, and spatial profile analysis to constrain the physical conditions of the molecular and atomic gas phases. Results. H2, Brg, and [Fe II] emission are detected in all structures studied. The H2 level populations are consistent with predominantly thermal, near-LTE excitation, with excitation temperatures in the range ~1860-2450 K. The [Fe II]/Brg ratios are well below the values expected for shock or X-ray dominated regions, favoring photoionization as the dominant excitation mechanism of the atomic gas. A clear spatial stratification is observed in both objects, with Brg peaking closer to the central star and H2 1-0S(1) and [Fe II] co-spatial at larger distances. The warm molecular masses derived from H2 emission lines are consistent with those estimated independently from H2 column densities. Conclusions. The diagnostics presented here support a photoevaporation scenario in which LISs are dense clumps being progressively ionized from outside by the radiation of central stars, while their H2 cores remain self-shielded. A slow internal shock may release Fe into the gas phase. These results extend the molecular mass trend established previously to a larger sample.

papers.title: Soft Excess Variability and a Test of X-ray Reprocessing in AGN Mrk 359 and NGC 4051 using NICER and TESS
papers.abstract: Continuum reverberation mapping of AGN accretion disks assumes that X-ray reprocessing drives the UV/optical variations on short timescales. This reprocessing should also produce an X-ray reflection spectrum, which could be the soft excess observed in many Type 1 AGN. Consequently, if the soft excess traces the reflected emission, the soft excess and optical light curves should be correlated because their variability is driven by the same illuminating X-ray continuum. We present results from a cross-correlation study using simultaneous NICER and TESS observations of $\sim$$30\mathrm{~days}$ for two AGN: Mrk 359 and NGC 4051. We performed time-resolved spectroscopic fits to the X-ray data using a model with power-law and soft-excess components. We find no strong correlation between the optical and soft excess light curves, with correlation coefficients $R(τ)$ $\sim$0.5 for both sources. The total X-ray light curve also shows a similarly poor correlation with the optical variations. However, we find a stronger correlation between the primary X-ray flux and the soft excess flux for both sources. The lack of correlation between the primary X-rays and soft-excess with the optical variations implies that simple linear X-ray reprocessing is not the dominant process driving the optical variability. Either an intervening reprocessor between the inner X-ray region and outer disc is present that dilutes the X-ray-optical correlation, or the optical variability is driven by other mechanisms such as extreme-UV reprocessing or intrinsic disk variability.

papers.title: Many-body Response to Spin-Independent and Spin-Dependent Dark Matter Scattering in a Superfluid Helium-3 Target
papers.abstract: The QUEST-DMC experiment employs an ultra-low-temperature superfluid $^3$He target in an effort to detect sub-GeV dark matter (DM). The low-momentum scattering of such light DM is sensitive to the many-body structure of superfluid $^3$He, making it necessary to account for the collective behaviour of the medium. We present a first-principles calculation of the DM scattering rate in this inherently quantum many-body medium for both spin-independent and spin-dependent interactions. The leading consequence of this many-body behaviour is a kinematic enhancement of the scattering rate arising from the Fermi-Dirac statistics of the ultra-low-temperature target. Accounting for this extends the projected reach to lower DM masses for both spin-independent and spin-dependent interactions under the benchmark detector assumptions considered here. The resulting sensitivity improvement becomes increasingly pronounced as the detector threshold drops into the sub-eV regime. It is negligible at the conventional readout threshold of approximately $31$ eV, but becomes significant at the $0.51$ eV benchmark threshold for SQUID-based readout. Specifically, at this threshold, incorporating the many-body response extends the higher-energy recoil tail and improves the projected low-mass reach by approximately $2.5\%$ relative to the single-atom approximation. This improvement becomes more pronounced at lower thresholds. Reaching a threshold of $5$ meV could further extend the sensitivity of QUEST-DMC into the realm of sub-MeV DM.

papers.title: Searching for magnetic field changes in the central compact object 1E 1207.4-5209 in two decades of X-ray spectra
papers.abstract: The central compact object (CCO) 1E 1207.4-5209 is remarkable in that its X-ray spectrum shows clear absorption features at ~0.7 and 1.4 keV. Attributing these features to electron cyclotron resonance, the implied surface magnetic field is B~(7-8)x10^10 G, which agrees approximately with the field inferred from the spin properties of the pulsar. Here we examine all XMM-Newton EPIC pn spectra from more than 30 observations of 1E 1207.4-5209 from 2001-2020. We model the rotation phase-averaged and phase-resolved spectra with a two blackbody and multiple absorption line model, focusing on potential changes in the absorption lines which would correspond to changes in the magnetic field that could be related to the pulsar's possible spin glitch in 2015 and recent detection in radio. We find the phase-averaged spectral parameters, and by implication the magnetic field, are constant across nearly 20 years of data, while some parameters characterizing the phase-resolved spectra vary with rotation phase. The spectral line energies and widths (e.g., E_1~0.66 keV and full width of 0.34 keV) imply the magnetic field distribution across the X-ray emitting regions spans the range B~(6-11)x10^10 G, with the highest fields being visible during the declining phase of the pulsations of 1E 1207.4-5209.

papers.title: Gravitational-wave hierarchical inference from population samples
papers.abstract: Standard approaches to gravitational-wave population inference require evaluating the probability density of the population model. While appropriate for models composed of exact functional forms, this approach is not compatible with state-of-the-art astrophysical predictions from population-synthesis codes, which simulate samples from astrophysical models whose densities are unknown. We present an approach that solely requires samples and never density evaluations of the targeted population model. Key technical ingredients include efficient surrogates for the single-event likelihoods and detection probability, together with an efficient sampling strategy. Using detections up to GWTC-5.0, we validate the method against standard inference with a parametric model, showcase its flexibility on a simulated population including hierarchical mergers, and present a realistic application to a grid of astrophysical population-synthesis simulations with five formation channels. This work paves the way toward a direct comparison of astrophysical models and gravitational-wave data.

papers.title: Effects of Environment on the Star Formation Histories and Shapes of Simulated Galaxies
papers.abstract: We investigate how environment is connected to the formation times and three-dimensional stellar shapes of galaxies using the FIREbox cosmological volume simulation. We analyze 1720 resolved galaxies at $z=0$ spanning stellar masses $M_\star\approx5\times10^6$ to $5\times10^{11}\,M_\odot$ and environments ranging from isolated galaxies to groups in $\sim10^{13}\,M_\odot$ halos. We quantify environment using the Perturbation Index (PI), which measures the cumulative tidal influence of neighboring galaxies relative to each galaxy's own binding force. We measure formation times from cumulative star formation histories and shapes from intrinsic stellar axis ratios. Formation times depend most strongly on stellar mass, but below $10^{10}\,M_\odot$, galaxies in more strongly perturbing environments formed their stars earlier, most clearly in the late-time star formation of low-mass galaxies. Galaxies in these environments also have larger minor-to-major axis ratios at all masses: more spherical at low and intermediate mass and thicker along the minor axis at high mass. A partial-correlation analysis shows that, below $10^8\,M_\odot$, the environment-shape correlation is no longer significant at fixed formation time, whereas between $10^8$ and $10^{10}\,M_\odot$ a modest correlation remains. Above $10^{10}\,M_\odot$, the weak environment-shape correlation is not explained by formation time. Below $10^{10}\,M_\odot$, high-PI galaxies also have lower halo masses at fixed stellar mass; at fixed halo mass, environment is only weakly correlated with formation time and shape, whereas formation time and shape remain correlated. We therefore predict that, at fixed stellar mass, dwarf galaxies in stronger tidal environments should appear rounder in projection, with the difference largely tracking the ages of their stellar populations.

papers.title: Augmenting Galaxy Catalogues using Machine Learning in the FLAMINGO Simulations
papers.abstract: Hydrodynamic simulations are instrumental in the analysis of observations such as galaxy clustering used for the estimation of cosmological parameters. However, for these purposes, the simulations need both a large box size and high resolution, which is computationally prohibitive. In this work we use the connection between galaxies and their host dark matter halos to populate dark-matter-only simulations, using data from the FLAMINGO simulations suite. We employ the Extremely Randomized Trees algorithm to model the connection between the mass profile, history and environment of dark matter halos and the probability distribution of the stellar mass of the galaxy contained in the halo. We use halos matched between a dark-matter-only simulation and the corresponding hydrodynamical simulation to train a model for centrals. For satellites, we employ a Gaussian Processes emulator that simultaneously optimises the hyperparameters of a model and selects for the dark matter features that are predictive of the stellar mass while being insensitive to the differences between the hydrodynamic and dark-matter-only simulations, then train a model on only these features. We then apply these models to produce a new galaxy catalogue for the 2.8 Gpc FLAMINGO-10k dark-matter-only simulation as a product of this work. We demonstrate that this catalogue reproduces the statistics of the galaxy-halo connection predicted by the smaller volume hydrodynamical simulation on which the model was trained, including the stellar mass function, stellar mass-dark matter mass relation, 2-point correlation functions and correlations between stellar mass and dark matter concentration, half mass radius and dark matter mass within 3 Mpc.

papers.title: Exoplanets are predominately aligned with exo-Kuiper Belts
papers.abstract: The architectures of planetary systems encode their formation and dynamical histories. In the Solar System, the near alignment of planetary orbits, the Kuiper Belt, and the Sun's equator supports planet formation in a rotating disk of gas and dust. However, some exoplanet systems show planets on orbits misaligned with their host stars or other planets, raising the question of whether misalignments are primordial or produced by post-formation dynamics. We present the first population-level constraints on the mutual inclinations of 32 planets in 16 systems relative to debris disks. We find that planets across orbital distances from 0.1 to 100 AU are predominantly aligned with the debris disks within 10 deg (30/32 planets). The alignment holds across systems spanning tens of million years to a few gigayears in age. These results indicate that the aligned architecture of the Solar System is representative of the birth conditions of exoplanet systems.

papers.title: The Full-Shape Analysis of the Fading Dark Sector Model
papers.abstract: We analyze the Fading Dark Sector (FDS) model, which is motivated by string theory and in which the fading of the dark sector is driven by a scalar field. The model is specified by two $O(1)$ numbers $(c,c')$ that parametrize the logarithmic derivatives of the dark energy and dark matter densities with respect to the field in Planck units. In previous work, we showed that this model provides a good fit to the DESI BAO, CMB, and SN datasets. Here, we extend that analysis to include the DESI DR1 full-shape galaxy power spectrum, which adds information about the time evolution of cosmic structure and provides an independent consistency check of the FDS model. We find that, when the DESI DR1 full-shape data are combined with CMB+DESI DR2 BAO+DES-Dovekie, the FDS model outperforms the Chevallier-Polarski-Linder (CPL) $w_0$-$w_a$ parameterization by $Δχ^2_{\rm MAP}=-4$ at equal parameter count and is preferred over $Λ$CDM at $4.1σ$. The inferred values of $(c,c')$ with the full-shape data are unchanged from our previous analysis, so this improvement indicates that FDS makes a prediction for the growth of structure that captures the observed growth history better than the $w_0$-$w_a$ parameterization.

papers.title: The Gravitational Wave Foreground from Galactic Cataclysmic Variables in LISA
papers.abstract: Electromagnetic observations have been the primary medium for studying cataclysmic variable (CV) systems, capitalizing on the invaluable opportunity they present to study binary stellar evolution and accretion. The launch of the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) mission, however, will enable a multi-messenger perspective of the population. We extend previous work to explore the gravitational wave (GW) spectra sourced by a local and Galactic population of CVs. Using the Bayesian LISA Inference Package (BLIP), we simulate LISA data containing these CV populations to understand their impact and our ability to jointly model CV and double white dwarf (DWD) GW spectra. While we find that a local CV population has negligible effect on the LISA datastream, a Galactic CV population will have a signal-to-noise ratio of approximately 76, depending on the characteristics of the DWD population present, and will bias existing DWD spectral models if ignored. Current approaches struggle to accurately recover both populations' respective spectra, calling for the creation of multi-component spectral models that include GW contributions from both CVs and DWDs. These results point toward a promising future for the study of CVs with LISA.

papers.title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). Enhancing deep-learning models: the impact of image processing and training data selection for strong-lens detection
papers.abstract: Euclid is expected to discover ~$10^5$ galaxy-galaxy strong gravitational lenses across ~14,000deg$^2$, requiring automated searches with high completeness and low false-positive rates. Despite advances in deep learning, the effects of training-set composition, image representation, and preprocessing on survey-scale detection remain poorly understood. We present an ablation study of the convolutional neural network used in the ECLIPSE strong-lens detection pipeline, evaluating different training configurations on a fixed test set. Using simulated and real Euclid data, we compare VIS-only and pseudo-RGB representations, FITS and JPEG formats, training-set composition, hard-negative selection, and multi-stage training. We also assess ensembling on ~67 million DR1 cutouts. Training-set composition and strategy strongly affect high-Recall performance. Omitting simulation based pre-training reduces high-Recall weighted average Precision by 83.7% for VIS-only and 74.5% for pseudo-RGB models. Negative-sample selection also substantially affects performance, while FITS yields modest gains over JPEG at high Recall (~2-5%). On DR1, the logit-mean ensemble improves average Precision by 28.0% and 39.9% over the individual VIS-only and pseudo-RGB models. Among ~70,000 candidates selected for visual inspection, it recovers 11,256 unique grade A (secure) and B (probable) lenses, compared with 9650 and 10,395 for the individual models. The branches show complementary ranking preferences, particularly for lenses benefiting from near-infrared information. Careful training-set design, realistic negatives, and multi-band ensembling improve survey-scale searches. Our final ensemble achieves ~80% Recall at the operational selection threshold, outperforming ablation models with higher global classification metrics and highlighting the need to optimise performance for realistic survey conditions.[Abridged]

papers.title: Properties of stellar disks and spheroids in simulated galaxies
papers.abstract: The optical morphology of a galaxy is determined by the relative importance of their disk and spheroidal components. Although the scaling laws of disk-dominated or spheroid-dominated galaxies have been studied in some detail, less attention has been paid to the properties of each component in galaxies where both coexist. We use a dynamical decomposition of 3452 galaxies from the TNG100 simulations with stellar masses in the range $10 \leq \log_\mathrm{10}(M_*/M_\odot) \leq 12$ to study how, at given mass, the properties of a spheroid are altered by the presence of a disk, and vice versa. We define spheroids as the non-rotating component made up of all stars in retrograde motion, plus an equal number of co-rotating stars mirrored in angular momentum and energy. Disks simply consist of the remainder of (co-rotating) stars. We find that disk properties (rotation speed, size, formation time) depend sensitively on the mass of the spheroidal component and therefore of the total mass of the galaxy in which both reside. At given mass, disks rotate faster, are more extended, and form their stars earlier as the mass of the spheroidal component increases. On the other hand, at fixed mass, the properties of spheroids are less sensitive to the presence of a disk. Roughly speaking, the classical bulges of simulated disk galaxies closely resemble ellipticals of similar stellar mass. The apparent structural invariance of spheroids to the presence of a disk is somewhat surprising, but it likely results because disks form out of high angular momentum material which surrounds the spheroid and thus have less dynamical influence on a spheroid's structure.

papers.title: HydróDex: gotta match 'em all!
papers.abstract: We present a comprehensive hydrodynamic classification of stationary fluid profiles in first-order phase transitions within the constant-sound-speed model, a physically motivated extension of the standard bag model that allows the sound speeds in front of and behind the wall, $c_+$ and $c_-$, to differ. Solving the matching conditions at the bubble wall and evolving the profile in the surrounding plasma, we systematically identify and classify all the possible stationary solutions. The classification recovers all previously known direct and inverse detonation, deflagration, and hybrid solutions, while revealing a new class of stationary configurations, termed mixed hybrids, featuring rarefaction waves on both sides of the wall and oppositely directed fluid flows. For a sufficiently pronounced hierarchy $c_+ > c_-$, the classification in terms of the wall velocity $ξ_w$ and the asymptotic strength parameter $α_N$ further exhibits degenerate regions in parameter space, where multiple distinct stationary profiles correspond to the same physical inputs $(ξ_w,α_N)$. This non-uniqueness arises as the parametrization discards thermodynamic information and is resolved once the underlying microphysics is specified. We also compute the kinetic-energy budget and the associated acoustic gravitational-wave spectra within the sound-shell model, finding that mixed-hybrid solutions, despite their oppositely directed flows, introduce no additional spectral feature, and their spectra can be closely mimicked by ordinary direct or inverse hybrids with very different fluid profiles. Finally, we release HydróDex, a public code that implements the complete hydrodynamic classification, fluid-profile construction, kinetic-energy budget, and gravitational-wave calculation.

papers.title: Astrometric microlensing by isolated black holes in the Roman Galactic Bulge Time Domain Survey
papers.abstract: Most of the hundred million stellar-mass black holes (BHs) expected in the Milky Way are predicted to be isolated. Characterizing this BH population will provide insights into stellar evolution and supernova explosion physics. The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope Galactic Bulge Time Domain Survey (GBTDS) will enable the detection of isolated BHs through astrometric microlensing, apparent stellar position shifts caused by deflection of distant starlight. We combine a Galactic model, stellar population synthesis model, BH initial--final mass relation, and kick velocity distribution to simulate events caused by isolated BH lenses. We assess the expected yield, sensitivity, characterization potential, and signal characteristics of these events to inform GBTDS search strategies. We predict $487 \pm 37$ isolated-BH microlensing events with detectable astrometric signals, 82% of which have impact parameters beyond 2 Einstein radii and consequently have small or undetectable photometric signals. Standard astrometric fits yield unit weight errors > 1.2 for 18% and > 2 for 2% of these events. Sensitivity peaks for 5-6$M_\odot$ BHs and is limited by the five-year GBTDS baseline. Weak microlensing parallax constraints limit BH mass precision, but events with Einstein timescales > 100 days and angular Einstein radii > 1.2 mas have high BH lens probabilities within our Galactic model. Wide-separation astrometric microlensing offers an independent discovery channel for isolated BHs beyond photometrically selected events. Realizing this opportunity requires dedicated multi-season GBTDS searches, joint astrometric and photometric modeling, and accounting for other astrometric variability. Although precise individual masses are challenging for these events, probabilistic lens classification could lead to Galactic abundance constraints on the population of isolated BHs.

papers.title: Effect of galaxy-informed merger timescales on massive black hole binaries in LISA
papers.abstract: Over a decade of direct N-body simulations tell us that massive black hole binary (MBHB) merger timescales are strongly dependent on the structural and kinematic properties of the host galaxy merger remnant. The physical stages of stellar scattering and gravitational wave (GW) emission of MBH coalescence occur below the resolution limit of most cosmological simulations, requiring post-processing to achieve accurate merging times. We apply a recently developed galaxy-informed merger timescale for MBHBs to the Romulus25 simulation and compare with current MBH merger rate and event rate estimates for the upcoming Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA). We find a median stellar scattering time of ~ 10^8.2 yr^-1, roughly an order of magnitude faster than those produced by timescales that rely on extrapolations of the stellar density profile. We predict a merger rate of ~ 11.5 yr^-1 corresponding to 46 merger events over a 4-year LISA mission. We also investigate the importance of the relative orbital inclination of the MBHB with respect to the host galaxy and of nuclear star cluster (NSC) modeling, finding that the quickest merger events correspond to MBHBs that counterrotate and galaxies assigned to host NSCs, which may be important for host galaxy identification in the multi-messenger era.

papers.title: Full-shape analysis of the Lyman-alpha forest power spectrum and bispectrum: validation on simulations
papers.abstract: The Lyman-$α$ (LyA) forest of neutral hydrogen provides a large-volume, high-resolution map of cosmological fluctuations from optical spectra at high redshift. To extract more information from the currently observing Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI), we derive an effective field theory (EFT) model for joint full-shape analyses of the LyA forest data. It combines the one-loop power spectrum of the LyA forest (FF), and of its cross-correlation with dark-matter halos, used as proxies for high-redshift quasars (FQ), with the tree-level bispectrum of the LyA forest (FFF). Importantly, the bispectrum breaks the LyA-specific degeneracy between the mean flux and the amplitude of the power spectrum. We validate our theory framework on idealized large-volume LyA forest mocks painted onto the AbacusSummit N-body simulation suite at redshift z=2.5. Fitting scales up to $k_\mathrm{max}^{FF\,(FQ)}=0.6\,(0.3)\,h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$ in the power spectrum and $k_\mathrm{max}^{FFF}=0.1\,h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$ in the bispectrum, our full-shape analysis yields unbiased constraints on the cosmological parameters in simulations. For a fully sampled flux field in a simulated volume of $V=8\,h^{-3}\,{\rm Gpc}^3$, we measure the Hubble constant, $H_0$, to $0.6\%$, the matter density, $Ω_{\rm m}$, to $1.6\%$ and the amplitude of matter clustering, $σ_8$, to $3.5\%$. Adding the bispectrum improves the constraints on $σ_8$ by $28\%$. We also demonstrate that the inclusion of the quasar one-loop power spectrum (QQ) and tree-level bispectrum (QQQ) further improves cosmological constraints by $\approx 35\%$ using $k_\mathrm{max}^{QQ,\,(QQQ)}=0.2,\,(0.08)\,h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$. Our theory framework enables full-shape analyses of high-redshift data from DESI and its successor DESI-II, enhancing knowledge of the growth of structure of the Universe during matter-domination.

papers.title: Microscopic Realizability of Non-unique Bubble Hydrodynamics
papers.abstract: First-order phase transitions drive fluid motion that induces energy transport and gravitational-wave production. The flows are usually classified in terms of the wall velocity and the transition strength. We show that this description fails when the two phases have unequal sound speeds $c_\pm$. New mixed-hybrid profiles may appear, and for a strong hierarchy, $c_+\gg c_-$, where the phase behind the wall is much softer, heating or cooling ahead of the wall allow for the coexistence of distinct stationary flows at the same wall velocity and transition strength. This ambiguity is removed once thermodynamic normalization and entropy production are specified. We identify microscopic settings that realize these sound-speed hierarchies. In thermal plasmas it requires exponentially large mass-to-temperature ratios, whereas at finite density a conserved charge removes this obstruction, making dense matter its natural arena.

papers.title: WDM_GW_Wavelets: A fast, JAX-based Python implementation of the Wilson-Daubechies-Meyer wavelet transform for the time-frequency analysis of gravitational wave data
papers.abstract: This paper describes a JAX-based implementation of the Wilson-Daubechies-Meyer (WDM) time-frequency transformation, intended for use in gravitational-wave data analysis.
